source.title: CBD: API-Only LLM Black-Box Unlearning through Controlled Behavioral Divergence
source.authors: Zhi-Qiang Xie; Yi-Jing Lin; Zhi-Peng Gao; Dong In Kim

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates an API-only routing method and explicitly distinguishes reducing exposure through routing from removing information from the target model's parameters. It does not test recovery attacks against the unlearning methods it compares.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own unlearning and routing results, including targeted-knowledge accuracy and retained utility. It does not apply fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, or prompt-based recovery attacks after unlearning. Its discussion of earlier concealment work is not a new result.
record.test_reason: This is a new-method paper. CBD routes forget-related queries to a small reference model and leaves the target model unchanged. The paper reports only CBD's suppression and utility numbers against reimplemented baselines. It applies no fine-tuning, internal-edit, quantization or prompting recovery attack to any method. So no version's core question (is the knowledge still recoverable?) is tested. CBD by design never removes knowledge from the target. Its 'near chance' WMDP score is therefore interface-level gating, not evidence about unlearning depth.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that CBD gives a better unlearning-utility trade-off than eleven baselines in an API-only setting. It works by routing forget-related queries to a reference model. They state it reduces exposure at the service interface rather than erasing the target's parameters.
record.recipe_differences: CBD uses auxiliary-model behavioral divergence to route queries in an API-only setting; it does not edit the target model's weights or use the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Routing performance varies with the selected basis: DFB outperforms GPM, especially on larger ToFU forget splits. The paper also reports sensitivity to top-k, retain basis size, forget basis size, and LoRA rank; top-k has the largest effect, and LoRA rank the smallest.

fits_no_version.finding: An API-only router lowers WMDP accuracy to 25.68 with MMLU 52.67, without editing the target model. The authors state it reduces exposure rather than erasing parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Query routing to a reference model can gate access to targeted knowledge at the service interface while the target's knowledge remains intact.

fits_no_version.finding: In the authors' reimplementation on WMDP, the white-box baseline GA+KL suppresses hazardous accuracy to 26.44 but drops MMLU to 28.96. Gray-box ULD and Offset barely suppress it (49.35, 50.63).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suppression–utility trade-off of standard unlearning baselines on WMDP with Zephyr-7B, without any recovery attack.

record.problems: No recovery attack is evaluated, and the target model is not edited; results therefore show interface-level suppression rather than whether the target's stored knowledge can be recovered. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the tabulated results.
record.rows_left_out: The WMDP Table VI results for other method-by-domain cells and the ToFU forget01/forget05 results are not included; the record keeps the explicitly discussed WMDP comparisons and CBD's detailed ToFU forget10 results. Hyperparameter-sensitivity plots and training-step values are omitted because they do not test post-unlearning recovery.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover knowledge after CBD or any baseline; CBD does not alter the target, so deletion is not attempted.
No activation ablation or analysis of whether baseline methods block access rather than delete.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attack, including against the router.
CBD is not evaluated against any recovery attack, so no robustness claim is tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels (A supports, A limits_scope, C supports) are dropped. No recovery attack is run, so neither shallowness nor robustness is tested. Routing metrics describe the study's own design, not evidence for version C. A recovery-attack test would require attacking the router itself (e.g., paraphrase evasion), which is not done.

versions.untested_parts: CBD's targeted-knowledge accuracy and retained utility are evaluated, but the study does not test whether simple attacks recover knowledge. Its CBD method routes queries and leaves the target model unchanged.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning-set recovery attack is tested.

The paper describes and evaluates CBD's access-routing mechanism, which does not edit the target weights. It does not ablate an activation direction or test this mechanism on the other unlearning methods.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context recovery attack is tested.
CBD is not evaluated for resistance to the recovery attacks in the claim.

rows.subject: Zephyr-7B-beta with CBD (with DFB)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate overall hazardous-knowledge accuracy after CBD query routing.
rows.note: The authors describe this as near the random-guess level. CBD routes queries; it does not edit the target model.
rows.check: Study's own method compared with baselines. The target is unedited (routing only), so this is not a measure of whether a method removes knowledge as version A means.

rows.subject: Zephyr-7B-beta with CBD (with DFB)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate biology hazardous-knowledge accuracy after CBD query routing.
rows.note: The Table VI column layout supports assigning this value to CBD's biology result.
rows.check: Own-method result; routing, not unlearning of the target. No baseline stated (chance is 25).

rows.subject: Zephyr-7B-beta with CBD (with DFB)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate chemistry hazardous-knowledge accuracy after CBD query routing.
rows.note: The Table VI column layout supports assigning this value to CBD's chemistry result.
rows.check: 26.96 is near the 25 chance level, so 'partial' overstates the gap. It is also an own-method routing result.

rows.subject: Zephyr-7B-beta with CBD (with DFB)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate retained general capability after CBD query routing.
rows.note: The authors report preserved MMLU performance, with the retained-utility cost attributed to false-positive routing.
rows.check: Own-method utility; the drop from 59.01 to 52.67 comes from false-positive routing.

rows.subject: Zephyr-7B-beta with GA+KL
rows.operation_detail: Apply gradient-ascent unlearning with a retain KL term.
rows.note: The paper identifies this as the strongest white-box suppression result.
rows.check: Reimplemented baseline shown as a comparator to the authors' method; no recovery attack applied.

rows.subject: Zephyr-7B-beta with GA+KL
rows.operation_detail: Apply gradient-ascent unlearning with a retain KL term.
rows.note: The authors state that GA+KL's MMLU accuracy drops to 28.96.
rows.check: Comparator baseline. It shows GA+KL's utility collapse (MMLU 28.96 vs 59.01), but no attack is tested.

rows.subject: Zephyr-7B-beta with ULD
rows.operation_detail: Apply logit-difference unlearning.
rows.note: The authors describe the gray-box baselines as achieving almost no hazardous-knowledge suppression.
rows.check: Comparator baseline (ULD barely suppresses: 49.35 vs 50.95); method comparison only.

rows.subject: Zephyr-7B-beta with Offset
rows.operation_detail: Apply offset unlearning.
rows.note: The authors describe the gray-box baselines as achieving almost no hazardous-knowledge suppression.
rows.check: Comparator baseline (Offset 50.63 vs 50.95); method comparison only.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B-Chat with CBD (with DFB)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate forget-set answer overlap after CBD query routing.
rows.note: The paper reports the forget-set value close to the retrained reference.
rows.check: Own-method ToFU result; routing, not target unlearning.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B-Chat with CBD (with DFB)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate forget-set answer probability after CBD query routing.
rows.note: Lower answer probability indicates less recovery of the reference answer.
rows.check: Own-method ToFU result.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B-Chat with CBD (with DFB)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate retained model utility after CBD query routing.
rows.note: The authors state that retained-side metrics stay close to the target because non-rerouted retained queries reach the unchanged target.
rows.check: Own-method utility result.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: CBD yields overall hazardous accuracy 25.68 against the stated chance level of 25 while reporting MMLU accuracy 52.67; recovery attacks were not tested (W1, W5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: CBD leaves the target unchanged and achieves its reported results by routing queries; the study does not show that the underlying target knowledge is deleted or test recovery attacks (W1, W5, R1-R8).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The paper states that CBD routes unlearning-related prompts away from the unchanged target LLM rather than erasing target parameters, and reports routing performance (R1-R8).
